name: Rule 24: Person changed data or a table's definition
summary: Medium. A person (in USER, not a service user) ran WRITE or DDL on a known object with a role that has no OWNERSHIP reach on it (data_use(role)[1][object] lacks "own"); one finding per user and object: statement counts, the most used role, last day. access.py:6668-6678

name: Rule 25: Service user used from an interactive client
summary: High. A service user (is_service) has activity rows whose CLIENT is in INTERACTIVE (Snowflake UI, SnowSQL, Snowflake CLI); one finding per service user: queries per client label, tables, last day. access.py:6663-6664,5192-5198

name: Rule 26: Admin role used to read or change data
summary: High. Activity rows whose ROLE_NAME is in ADMIN on a known object; one finding per user and admin role: objects read, objects changed (action not READ), first three names. access.py:6665-6666,5199-5203

name: Rule 27: First access to a table in the last 7 days
summary: Low. Per user and object: the first day on the object is within the last NEW_DAYS (7) days of the snapshot and the user had activity before cut - NEW_DAYS (not a new user); detail adds "sensitive" for tagged objects. access.py:6657,5179-5183

name: Rule 28: Unusual volume on a table
summary: Medium. Per user and object with at least 5 active days: the busiest day has >= SPIKE[1] (50) queries and more than SPIKE[0] (3) x the median day. access.py:6684-6691

name: Activity read window (incremental)
summary: Window = ACTIVITY_DAYS (60) back from now, cut at UTC midnight (TIMESTAMP_TZ literal, not the session time zone); rows of an earlier read are kept up to the day before its last day, and that day onwards is read again (ACCESS_HISTORY lags up to 3 hours). Same in SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT activity() (sql/1_setup.sql:794-802).

name: App's own queries left out of activity
summary: The app's own queries are left out of the activity. Both names are settings: QUERY_TAG (env, default 'access-explorer', access.py:102) is set on the app's connection (sf.py:35); STREAMLIT_APP (env, default ST_ACCESS_EXPLORER, read into APP_ST, access.py:103) is the app inside Snowflake. activity_sql and ACT_BASE drop QUERY_HISTORY rows with that tag, rows whose StreamlitName is that app, and the TBL_ACCESS_ tables SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT writes (access.py:1405-1411, 4440-4441); quotes and backslashes are escaped first (access.py:1382, quoted() at 4493). The procedure takes both from !define QUERY_TAG / STREAMLIT_APP (sql/1_setup.sql:210-211, 570-576); local .env, sis/.env and settings.local.sql must agree.

name: Activity tab counts
summary: activity(name, what, user): queries per day over ACTIVITY_DAYS ending at the snapshot day for an object, user, role, app (APP) or scope (OBJECT_NAME under name + '.'), totals by user/role/client/statement/object split into read/write/ddl, one row per user+role+client+object+statement+action with hours per UTC hour (weekdays), weekend and weekend_hours, first_day, kind and interactive; counts are per action, so a MERGE that reads and changes a table counts twice.

name: Grant path behind a use
summary: used_path(user, role, object, action): user -> shortest chain to the role used -> shortest data_use chain to a holder of a privilege that fits the action (READ_PRIVS for READ, else WRITE_PRIVS or OWNERSHIP) -> object; None when the role reaches no such grant now (admin role, grant gone).

name: ACTIVITY_DAYS
summary: Days of table activity read and shown (env ACTIVITY_DAYS, default 60)

name: QUERY_TAG
summary: env QUERY_TAG, default 'access-explorer': query tag on the app's own connection (sf.py:35), left out of the activity. Same value as !define QUERY_TAG (settings.sql:19) and QUERY_TAG in .env / sis/.env

name: INTERACTIVE
summary: Clients where people type queries (env INTERACTIVE_CLIENTS; default Snowflake UI, SnowSQL, Snowflake CLI); rule 25

name: CLIENTS
summary: SESSIONS client id (version cut) -> short label (Snowflake UI -> Snowsight, PythonConnector -> Python, ...)

name: SPIKE
summary: Rule 28 thresholds: (3 x the median day, at least 50 queries)

name: NEW_DAYS
summary: Rule 27: first access within the last 7 days

name: MAX_ACTIVITY
summary: Activity rows sent (2000); the counts above them cover all rows

name: Rule 29: Streamlit app shows its owner's sensitive data to people who cannot read it
summary: High. Per Streamlit app (kinds STREAMLIT) whose owner roles (OWNERSHIP) read sensitive objects, per role holding USAGE on the app: users reaching that role who cannot read some of those objects through their own roles (user_reads) -> one finding on the holder role: app, owner, sensitive objects, users. Fix: revoke the app's USAGE from the role. access.py:5703-5718, app_exposure access.py:5663-5676

name: Streamlit app runs with its owner's rights
summary: app_exposure(app): owner = roles with OWNERSHIP on the app; sensitive = what the owner reads that is sensitive (columns, [] = whole object); holders = roles with USAGE on the app -> users reaching them; exposed = per user the sensitive objects they cannot read through their own roles (PUBLIC included); None without an owner

name: Activity hours in UTC, business time as an offset
summary: activity_sql groups per UTC day and keeps HOURS = {UTC hour: queries} (access.py:1388-1389, 970-975); activity() splits them into weekday hours and weekend_hours (access.py:5332-5337); the UI counts off-hours as weekend queries plus weekday hours outside [start, end) after shifting by a UTC offset (offOf, web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:25-26); default start-end from WORK_HOURS 7-19 (access.py:114, server.py:2364)

name: Activity view by object type
summary: activity_page picks the view from the object's kind: STREAMLIT -> app (rows where APP = name), DATABASE / SCHEMA -> scope (every object under the name), WAREHOUSE -> who ran queries on it from the usage read (warehouse_use, no ACCESS_HISTORY), else object; app and scope get no grant-path graph

name: Copy-only SQL behind the Activity tab
summary: query_sql(name, what, first, last): read-only SELECT over ACCESS_HISTORY x QUERY_HISTORY x SESSIONS listing every query id, time, user, role, statement, object and client in the window (no query text), filter per what (object, user, role, app by StreamlitName, scope by LIKE prefix), quotes doubled; the app never runs it

name: WORK_HOURS
summary: Business hours start-end (env WORK_HOURS, default 7-19, end exclusive); sent as work to the Activity tab, which shifts them from UTC with its business-time slider

name: Which SQL a page shows to run yourself
summary: Per page and params, the read-only ACCOUNT_USAGE queries behind it with SET lines filled in (grants from access_queries files, activity per section, tags, policies, PUBLIC, admin holders, dormant users); the app never runs them. Names from the link are kept on one line with backslashes and quotes escaped (one_line, quoted, lit), so no name can start a statement of its own. See logic/page-sql.md.

name: SQL behind each Activity section
summary: One query per Activity section over ACCESS_HISTORY x QUERY_HISTORY x SESSIONS for the name and window, default business hours, TZ_HOURS=0; sent as section_sql. See logic/page-sql.md.

name: STREAMLIT_APP (APP_ST)
summary: env STREAMLIT_APP, default ST_ACCESS_EXPLORER, read into APP_ST: the app inside Snowflake; queries whose QUERY_TAG StreamlitName is it are left out of the activity (access.py:1406, 4440). Same value as !define STREAMLIT_APP (settings.sql:17) and sis/.env

name: CSV

name: CSV export can be turned off
summary: CSV=0: serve_csv refuses with ApiError 403 csv_off in both versions (FastAPI *.csv routes, st_react.answer), and the React app hides every CSV button from meta.csv; the screen stays visible, so app access remains the real control

name: STATEMENT_TIMEOUT
summary: env STATEMENT_TIMEOUT, default 300 s, 0 = Snowflake's own: sent as STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS with each statement (sf.limit, none for a CALL), in every mode; the procedure's own limit is settings.sql STATEMENT_TIMEOUT (README.md:214, .env.example:41-42, sis.env.example:24-26)

name: WORKERS
summary: env WORKERS, default 3: heavy reads at once on the one connection or session (snapshot tables, Direct-mode ACCOUNT_USAGE reads); SHOW_THREADS (16) for the light SHOW waves; the procedure's own is settings.sql WORKERS (README.md:213, .env.example:43-44, sis.env.example:27-29)

name: ACTIVITY
summary: env ACTIVITY, default 1: 0 reads no ACCESS_HISTORY (object use, activity with QUERY_HISTORY / SESSIONS) in Direct mode and in the snapshot read; SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT has settings.sql ACTIVITY; the cache key gets _noactivity (README.md:215, .env.example:45-46, sis.env.example:30-31)

name: HIERARCHY
summary: env HIERARCHY, default 1: 0 skips the rule checks that walk role paths (WALKS: 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 14, 17-24, 29; rule 6 without its reader count); pages still walk (README.md:216, .env.example:47-48, sis.env.example:32-33)

name: Every statement has a time limit that says how to raise it
summary: STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS as a statement parameter, not ALTER SESSION (the same locally and inside Snowflake); none on the SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT CALL (a cut CALL would leave its run RUNNING). A timeout (error 000630, access.timed_out) raises TimeoutError '<step>: stopped after 5 min (STATEMENT_TIMEOUT=300); set STATEMENT_TIMEOUT=600 for 10 minutes', or says a lower warehouse / account limit stoppe

name: Independent reads run side by side
summary: each(): light SHOW waves SHOW_THREADS (16) at a time, heavy reads WORKERS (3) at a time on the one connection; answers in order, a failure as its exception, so one unreadable role skips only itself. SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT: SHOW / fallback statements as async child jobs BATCH (16) at a time (many), heavy INSERTs at most WORKERS at once (later / wait), async off for the run when its probe fails (async_o

name: ACTIVITY=0 reads no ACCESS_HISTORY
summary: ACTIVITY=0: snapshot() reads no OBJECT_USE / ACTIVITY table, live() probes neither ACCESS_HISTORY nor SESSIONS (access.py:1007-1008), SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT skips both steps; sources SKIPPED, note 'skipped (ACTIVITY=0)', rules 24-28 skipped (skipped_rules), the Activity tabs and Granted vs used say so (server.note_info, server.py:559-562); its own cache key (_noactivity)

name: HIERARCHY=0 skips the rules that walk role paths
summary: HIERARCHY=0: the checks in WALKS (3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 14, 17-24, 29) do not run, rule 6 runs without its reader count, rule_rows counts no 'who loses access'; skipped_rules() lists them as 'skipped (HIERARCHY=0)', so Risks & fixes and Home show them as skipped, not passing (server.py:2692-2721, Risks.tsx:86-90); pages still walk

name: One ACCESS_HISTORY read for object use and activity
summary: history_sql scans ACCESS_HISTORY once (A0, from the earlier cut) for both; each part keeps its own cut; PART = USE / ACT rows split by history_rows (Direct mode) or one INSERT ALL in SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT history(). If the shared read fails, each step reads alone (one failing read fails only its step); not after a timeout (a read apart scans the same rows under the same limit)

name: Object use read incrementally by week
summary: use_start: window USE_DAYS back in whole ISO weeks; an earlier read's weeks are kept but its last two, which are read again (ACCESS_HISTORY lags up to 3 hours), so a refresh reads one or two weeks and gives the rows of a full read; SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT object_use does the same in SQL (test_sql.test_object_use_weeks)

name: Same snapshot run: nothing read again
summary: snapshot(old=cache.last): when the last OK RUN_ID equals the held data's and that data has the current shape (every table a list, no RUN_ID column, HOURS parsed), it is returned after the one TBL_ACCESS_RUN query; a new run reads every table again (test_server.test_same_run)

name: A load says what it is doing
summary: Reads report lines through a.say() into the sink set by a.progress() (a context variable, handed to each()'s threads); a heartbeat adds "Still working after N min: <steps>" every BEAT s; a.step() times build steps; server.tracked keeps them per cache key (last 200) for GET /api/progress (also job: the background refresh) and prints them when LOG_LINES; uvicorn leaves /api/progress out of its log (quiet_log); inside Snowflake st_react.shown writes them; server.built steps: "Building the role graph", "Checking the rules", "Working out what each fix changes", "Saving the rule results", "Preparing the pages" (server.py:192-205); a page with no answer yet shows kit.tsx Waiting

name: Snapshot data tables keep no Time Travel
summary: TBL_ACCESS_ data tables are created with DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 0 and the RETENTION_* (may fail) statements set it on existing tables: each run deletes older runs' rows, so Time Travel would only store copies

name: One read per cache key at a time
summary: lock(key): an RLock per key (LOCKS, guarded by LOCK), so a read of one key never waits on another (shared and My access load side by side); SQL_LOCK serialises the one .cache/access.duckdb writer; drop() keeps the memory copy in OLD for last()

name: Every Snowflake read kept as a part; a load resumes
summary: Stage 1 keeps each read (heavy ACCOUNT_USAGE read, SHOW wave, snapshot table) as .cache/reads/<key>/<label>-<hash>.parquet, written by pyarrow, else duckdb (neither: no parts, a load reads everything; cache.py:368-376); the next load reads only the missing parts and, in a wave, only its timed-out statements; a part of a lost session is never kept; prune() drops parts a whole load did not ask for; the last OK snapshot run is always asked, never answered from a part (the answer is kept for --build); parts are read again only on Rebuild snapshot / Read Snowflake again or run.py --export --fresh; stage 2 needs no Snowflake

name: A refresh runs in the background; old data stays until the new is built
summary: Rebuild snapshot / Read Snowflake again: one JOB at a time, read under KEY + ".new" with its own parts (kept for an hour after a failure, so the next refresh resumes), timed-out reads keep the old data, built, then cache.swap and compared(d) (What changed made while the replaced data is still built, business_rule:changes_at_refresh); a failure keeps the old data and the message in JOB; locally in a thread (BACKGROUND), inside Snowflake inline (app.py); the React indicator stops and says so when the server restarted during it

name: A page never waits behind a load
summary: load_shared takes LOAD without blocking for a page: busy -> 409 shared_loading; the React app makes the page inert and polls /api/progress until the load ends, then asks again; built() already did the first page's work (rule 17, breaks, sens, server.py:198-205), and a page still waiting shows Waiting (Loading… with its seconds, after 10 s a still-working hint)

name: Rule results kept across restarts
summary: Shared data in Snowflake mode: findings, rows, ro, breaks saved in .cache/<key>.rules.pkl with (build key, builtin, a.rules_stamp(), SERVER_STAMP); reused while the data, the settings access.py reads, access.py and server.py are unchanged; built() works out all four in the load and saves them (server.py:195-203)

name: Account-wide rule checks walk role path counts in DuckDB
summary: duck() builds role links, start roles and path counts per hop in an in-memory DuckDB once per data set; lose_all() answers who loses access for every fix edge in one query, read_shares() pre-counts what each role reaches; equal to the Python walk (test_duck_reach); without duckdb, with a role loop or past MAX_HOPS the Python walk runs

name: Rules 17 and 23 walk only roles they can flag
summary: read_shares() counts per role the data objects reached, read only, written / owned, owned and schema CREATE grants; readonly_writes and rule23 skip a role neither the name nor the behaviour heuristic can flag before walking it

name: Missing, NULL or unreadable data gives empty results plus a note
summary: tidy() fills missing columns, empties missing tables (SOURCES UNAVAILABLE), leaves out rows without names / day / action (missing_names) and notes missing snapshot columns (missing_columns); snapshot() and live() turn unreadable tables and refused SHOWs into notes; only a lost session (lost()) stops a load; note_info explains each key

name: No OK snapshot run: empty pages that say so, never kept
summary: snapshot(): no OK run, no RUN_ID, or TBL_ACCESS_RUN unreadable -> every table empty with NOTES no_run; cache.store keeps such a read in memory only (no .pkl, no SQL copy) and keep_prev never sets it aside as the previous snapshot

name: SESSIONS read only from a week before the first day
summary: activity_sql (and the same text in SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT) joins ACCOUNT_USAGE.SESSIONS created from 7 days before the first day read, not a year of sessions; a session open longer shows no client, so rule 25 may miss it

name: Each source: ACCOUNT_USAGE first, then INFORMATION_SCHEMA or SHOW
summary: live(): every ACCOUNT_USAGE view probed in one wave; a refused probe gives the fallback reason. Grants and users: ACCOUNT_USAGE, else SHOW ROLES / SHOW GRANTS TO|OF ROLE, SHOW USERS (access.py:1090-1104, 1178-1201); query history: ACCOUNT_USAGE (30 days), else INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY over 7 windows of 167 h (week(), 10,000 queries per call; access.py:766-772, 1203-1216); tags and policies: ACCOUNT_USAGE, else INFORMATION_SCHEMA per table up to TAG_FALLBACK_MAX (access.py:1236-1314); none readable -> UNAVAILABLE + note. mine(): ACCOUNT_USAGE grants / roles / user in one wave, SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE only when GRANTS_TO_ROLES fails; usage ACCOUNT_USAGE then INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY_BY_USER (access.py:812-829, 848-849, 873, 911-922). SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT AUTO does the same (fallback(), grants(), users(), usage(); sql/1_setup.sql:340-353, 365-395, 486-509, 513-544).

name: A timeout means busy, not unreadable
summary: slow(e) = TimeoutError or error 000630 (timed_out). A probe that timed out counts as readable, so the full read is tried, not the SHOW fallback (access.py:1002-1004; sql/1_setup.sql:350-351). A full ACCOUNT_USAGE read that timed out: Direct mode notes the source UNAVAILABLE (SHOW would be slower still) (access.py:1098-1099, 1186-1187); SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT fails the run instead (sql/1_setup.sql:388-389, 497-498). Refused (any other error) -> the fallback. A timed-out part is kept as failed and read again on the next load (cache.py:483, 501); a refresh with timed-out reads keeps the old data (server.py:3209-3212).

name: A lost session or no warehouse stops the load
summary: lost(e): ConnectionError, OperationalError / InterfaceError, errno 606 (no warehouse: every SELECT fails, SHOW still works) or 390111/390112/390114 (to verify). live() and mine() raise it after the probe wave instead of running SHOW fallbacks (access.py:999-1001, 827-829); a lost part is never kept (cache.py:473-474); the server answers 503 shared_unreadable / mine_unreadable with load_error(), which adds 'Set SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE in .env' for 000606 (server.py:225, 224-227, 295).

name: What changed is compared at refresh, while the replaced data is still built
summary: renew() swaps the new read in, then compared(d): only when cache.prev(KEY) exists and its shared_key is still in a.built does it build d and run diff_of(prev) under LOCK; else (a same-run refresh kept an older previous) the first open of What changed compares. A failure is said in the load log only. diff_of keeps one diff per data-set pair (a.cached) and, in Snowflake mode with a local cache, .cache/<key>.diff.pkl stamped (prev key, loaded key, builtin, rules_stamp, SERVER_STAMP) (server.py:2457-2474); a.diff(prev, prev_findings(prev), key, pairs=False) reuses the kept findings and built set (access.py:6114-6128).

name: What changed events name only their first people and objects
summary: a.diff: an event lists its first EVENT_NAMES (200) people and objects (sorted, nsmallest) with capped=True when cut; impact counts all (access.py:6148-6159). changes_page sends each event's first NAMES (20) people, objects and subjects plus subject=, and with subject= and a capped event adds 'Big changes name only their first 200 people and objects, so some about <subject> may be missing here' (server.py:2409, 2436-2437, 2442-2443).

name: Big graphs send combined boxes empty
summary: build_graph: with src (gsrc params) and more than LAZY (300) members over all combined boxes and lane boxes, the graph is big: boxes go out with counts only (lazy, a folded lane's role names in ids) and src; graph?of=<page>&group=<box> (only=) answers one box with up to MAX_MEMBERS (1000) members (server.py:733-736, 803-825, 3040-3051).

name: Crowded lanes of a big graph fold into one box
summary: fold_lanes: in a big graph, a lane with more than MAX_LANE (24) free roles becomes box lane:<i>, more than 24 people (users or stacked boxes, counted by size) lane:<i>:people; the start and selected box never fold, objects never; lines to members end at the box with the member count. Same idea as graphs.ts foldRoles on the client.

name: Map objects roll up per database
summary: map_graph: combine_tab(at=last lane) turns an objects lane over MAX_BOX (= MAX_OBJECTS, 12) into one box per database 'DB · N objects' (drill into the database); account-level objects and a database with one object stay single (server.py:921-951); once per data set (map_combined); params carry of=map so lazy boxes open through graph?of=map&group=; map?node=<id> answers one box's detail (server.py:2291-2293).

name: Admin paths capped per admin role and on the Object banner
summary: admin_paths: per admin role at most MAX_PATHS paths, shortest first (one shared cap would let SYSADMIN paths hide ACCOUNTADMIN); admin_holders: at most MAX_PATHS per grantee and admin role (access.py:2685-2695); Object page banner lists the first MAX_ADMIN_PATHS (20) user admin paths, admin_users and admin_total count all (server.py:1918, 1918, 1966).

name: Long tables are paged on the server
summary: window(p, key, n): slice(offset, offset+limit) from key= and limit= (PAGE by default, 0 = every row for CSV), offset reset past the end: Object users (m_offset), Sensitive objects / readers (o_offset, r_offset), What changed events (offset) (server.py:1930, 2569-2570, 2441). paged(p, rows): offset= / limit= (PAGE, at most 1000) for privs, access, held, grantees (server.py:1284-1288). Risks & fixes: FINDINGS_PAGE 100 (limit up to 500), counts and groups over every finding, one finding's fix via /api/finding?id= (server.py:2621, 2703, 2729). Review: REVIEW_PAGE 50 (limit up to 1000) (server.py:2799, 2859).

name: EVENT_NAMES
summary: 200: people and objects a What changed event lists

name: NAMES
summary: 20: people, objects and subjects sent per What changed event

name: LAZY
summary: 300 members over all combined boxes: a graph sends boxes empty

name: MAX_LANE
summary: 24 role boxes (or people) per lane of a big graph before it folds

name: MAX_ADMIN_PATHS
summary: 20 admin paths listed on the Object page banner

name: PAGE
summary: 50 rows per page of a server-paged table: paged() (privs, access, held, grantees) and window() (sensitive objects and readers, an object's users, What changed events)

name: FINDINGS_PAGE
summary: 100 findings per Risks & fixes answer (limit up to 500)

name: REVIEW_PAGE
summary: 50 rows per Review page (limit up to 1000)

name: reads.md
summary: Snowflake reads: ACCOUNT_USAGE -> INFORMATION_SCHEMA -> SHOW per source, timeouts (busy, not unreadable), lost session / no warehouse, server-side paging
